Σ_{p∈s} β_p Σ_i (−1)^i (I(front_{p,i}) − I(back_{p,i})) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q I(q).
For a test m-form γ, put I_γ(q) := ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy. By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply and hT at ω := dγ:
∂T(γ) = T(dγ) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{Q^{m+1}} dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy.

∫_{Q^{m+1}} dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy = Σ_i (−1)^i (I_γ(front_{p,i}) − I_γ(back_{p,i})).
Applying face_regroup's identity at I := I_γ yields ∂T(γ) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q I_γ(q). s' and β' do not depend on γ.

subproblems.title: Fubini and FTC on the unit cube: integrating one partial derivative over Q^{k+1}
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, i ∈ Fin (k+1), and let G : Euclid (k+1) → ℝ be C¹. Write Q^d := {y ∈ Euclid d : 0 < y_j < 1 for all j} (Lebesgue measure volume) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid k let ins_i(c, y') := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i c (WithLp.ofLp y')) ∈ Euclid (k+1), the point with i-th coordinate c and remaining coordinates y' in order. Then y ↦ DG(y)e_i is integrable on Q^{k+1}, and ∫_{Q^{k+1}} DG(y)e_i dy = ∫_{Q^k} G(ins_i(1, y')) dy' − ∫_{Q^k} G(ins_i(0, y')) dy'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 1)) (G : Euclid (k + 1) → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → IntegrableOn (fun y => fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) {y : Euclid (k + 1) | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1} ∧ ∫ y in {y : Euclid (k + 1) | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = (∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i (1 : ℝ) (WithLp.ofLp y)))) - ∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i (0 : ℝ) (WithLp.ofLp y)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 ("The cube identity") of the parent proof, for one coordinate i and one C¹ function. In this split the sibling cube_stokes applies it with G := G_i, the i-th coordinate of the divergence field. The frozen contract does not import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem, so the identity is proved, as in the parent proof, from Fubini and the one-variable fundamental theorem of calculus. Every lemma named below resolves under `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`.

Notation. For d ∈ ℕ: Q^d := {y ∈ Euclid d | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}; B^d := Set.pi univ (fun _ : Fin d => Ioo 0 1) ⊆ (Fin d → ℝ), the open box; C^d := Set.pi univ (fun _ : Fin d => Icc 0 1), the closed box. toLp := WithLp.toLp 2 and ofLp := WithLp.ofLp are mutually inverse, and (toLp x) j = x j. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. g(y) := DG(y)e_i = fderiv ℝ G y e_i.

1. Regularity. G is C¹ and 1 ≠ 0, so G is differentiable (ContDiff.differentiable) and y ↦ fderiv ℝ G y is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Applying a continuous family of continuous linear maps to the constant vector e_i is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply), so g is continuous.

2. Integrability (first conjunct). C^d is compact (isCompact_univ_pi with isCompact_Icc), so its image toLp '' C^d ⊆ Euclid d under the continuous map toLp (PiLp.continuous_toLp) is compact. Every y ∈ Q^d equals toLp (ofLp y) with ofLp y ∈ C^d, so Q^d ⊆ toLp '' C^d. A continuous function is integrable on a compact set (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact), hence on every subset (IntegrableOn.mono_set). With d = k + 1 and the function g this is the first conjunct.

3. Transport to boxes. For every d and every f : Euclid d → ℝ, ∫_{Q^d} f(y) dy = ∫_{B^d} f(toLp x) dx. Indeed toLp ⁻¹' Q^d = B^d (both say 0 < x j < 1 for every j), toLp is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp) and a measurable embedding (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin d → ℝ), whose coercion is toLp), so MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb applies. Apply this to the three integrals of the claim; since ofLp (toLp z) = z, it remains to prove
   (∗) ∫_{B^{k+1}} g(toLp x) dx = ∫_{B^k} G(toLp (insertNth i 1 z)) dz − ∫_{B^k} G(toLp (insertNth i 0 z)) dz.

4. Splitting off coordinate i. Let e := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) i : (Fin (k+1) → ℝ) ≃ᵐ ℝ × (Fin k → ℝ). Its inverse is e.symm (t, z) = Fin.insertNth i t z (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove_symm_apply, Fin.insertNthEquiv), and e.symm is measure preserving from volume.prod volume to volume (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, MeasurePreserving.symm). Moreover e.symm ⁻¹' B^{k+1} = Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k: insertNth i t z lies in B^{k+1} iff t ∈ Ioo 0 1 and z l ∈ Ioo 0 1 for every l (Fin.forall_iff_succAbove i, Fin.insertNth_apply_same, Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove). Put F(t, z) := g(toLp (insertNth i t z)). MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb for the measurable embedding e.symm gives ∫_{B^{k+1}} g(toLp x) dx = ∫_{Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k} F d(volume.prod volume).

5. Fubini. F is continuous on ℝ × (Fin k → ℝ) (Continuous.finInsertNth with continuous_fst and continuous_snd, then toLp and g). Hence F is integrable on the compact set Icc 0 1 ×ˢ C^k (IsCompact.prod) and so on its subset Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k, for volume.prod volume. By Measure.prod_restrict, (volume.restrict (Ioo 0 1)).prod (volume.restrict B^k) = (volume.prod volume).restrict (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k), so F is integrable for the product of the restricted measures, and integral_prod_symm gives ∫_{Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k} F = ∫_{z ∈ B^k} (∫_{t ∈ Ioo 0 1} F(t, z) dt) dz.

6. FTC in coordinate i. Fix z and put φ(t) := G(toLp (insertNth i t z)). First, toLp (insertNth i t z) = toLp (insertNth i 0 z) + t • e_i for every t: compare coordinates j (Fin.eq_self_or_eq_succAbove i j); at j = i both sides equal t, and at j = succAbove i l both equal z l, since e_i vanishes there (Fin.succAbove_ne). So t ↦ toLp (insertNth i t z) has derivative e_i at every t ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const e_i, then HasDerivAt.const_add). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt with the derivative of G at toLp (insertNth i t z)), φ has derivative fderiv ℝ G (toLp (insertNth i t z)) e_i = F(t, z) at every t. The map t ↦ F(t, z) is continuous (F composed with t ↦ (t, z)), hence interval integrable on [0, 1], and intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt gives ∫_0^1 F(t, z) dt = φ(1) − φ(0). As 0 ≤ 1, ∫_0^1 equals the integral over Ioc 0 1 (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le), which equals the integral over Ioo 0 1 for Lebesgue measure (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo). So ∫_{t ∈ Ioo 0 1} F(t, z) dt = G(toLp (insertNth i 1 z)) − G(toLp (insertNth i 0 z)).

7. Conclusion. For c ∈ {0, 1}, z ↦ G(toLp (insertNth i c z)) is continuous (Continuous.finInsertNth with a constant first argument), hence integrable on the compact C^k and on B^k ⊆ C^k. By integral_sub, the right-hand side of (∗) equals ∫_{B^k} (G(toLp (insertNth i 1 z)) − G(toLp (insertNth i 0 z))) dz. By step 6 and setIntegral_congr_fun (B^k is measurable: MeasurableSet.univ_pi with measurableSet_Ioo), this equals ∫_{z ∈ B^k} ∫_{t ∈ Ioo 0 1} F(t, z) dt dz. By steps 4 and 5, that is the left-hand side of (∗). So (∗) holds, and with step 3 so does the second conjunct. For k = 0, Fin 0 → ℝ is a single point, B^0 is all of it and has volume 1, and every step applies verbatim. ∎
proof_key_steps: g(y) = DG(y)e_i is continuous because G is C¹; Q^{k+1} lies in the compact set toLp '' [0,1]^{k+1}, so g is integrable on Q^{k+1}.
Transport each cube integral to the open box B^d ⊆ Fin d → ℝ with the measure-preserving embedding toLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp, setIntegral_preimage_emb).
Split off coordinate i with the measure-preserving map (t, z) ↦ insertNth i t z (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove); B^{k+1} pulls back to Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k.
Fubini (Measure.prod_restrict, integral_prod_symm) for the continuous integrand F(t, z) = g(toLp(insertNth i t z)), with the t-integral inside.
FTC in t: toLp(insertNth i t z) = toLp(insertNth i 0 z) + t e_i, so d/dt G(…) = F(t, z) and ∫_{Ioo 0 1} F(t, z) dt = G(…1…) − G(…0…).
Recombine with integral_sub and setIntegral_congr_fun to obtain the difference of the two face integrals.

subproblems.title: Cubical Stokes for one lattice cube from a divergence representation of dγ
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P (arbitrary), b : Fin P → ℤ, and let γ be any differential m-form on Euclid P. Write e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 ∈ Euclid P and toLp(b) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P. Put Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ Euclid (m+1), E := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) and, for i ∈ Fin (m+1), E'_i := (e_{ι(succAbove i l)})_{l ∈ Fin m}. Let G : Euclid (m+1) → Euclid (m+1) be C¹ with G(y)_i = (−1)^i γ(Φ y)(E'_i) for all y and i, and assume dγ(Φ y)(E) = trace DG(y) for all y, where d = exteriorDerivative and trace = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m+1)). Define the front and back faces Φ¹_i(y') := toLp(b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} and Φ⁰_i(y') := toLp(b) + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} for y' ∈ Euclid m, where 𝟙_{ι(i)} = Pi.single (ι i) 1 ∈ ℤ^P. With Q^d the open unit cube of Euclid d: ∫_{Q^{m+1}} dγ(Φ y)(E) dy = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (m+1)} (−1)^i (∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ¹_i y')(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ⁰_i y')(E'_i) dy').
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ι : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (b : Fin P → ℤ) (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → (∀ (y : Euclid (m + 1)) (i : Fin (m + 1)), G y i = (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun l => EuclideanSpace.single (ι (Fin.succAbove i l)) (1 : ℝ))) → (∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), exteriorDerivative γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, exteriorDerivative γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * ((∫ y in {y : Euclid m | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1 : Fin P → ℤ) k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ))) - ∫ y in {y : Euclid m | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 (the trace computation) and 4 ("Cubical Stokes") of the parent proof, for one index pair p = (ι, b). The hypotheses (H1)–(H3) on G are plain assumptions here (in the parent they are supplied by parent step 2); no declaration other than the sibling cube_partial_ftc is used. ι need not be monotone, γ needs no regularity, and only C¹ regularity of G is used. Uses the sibling cube_partial_ftc (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfrcb_cube_partial_ftc).

Notation. a := toLp (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P; w_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1; Φ(y) := a + Σ_j y j • w_j; E := (w_j)_{j ∈ Fin (m+1)}. For i ∈ Fin (m+1): E'_i := (l ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (ι (Fin.succAbove i l)) 1), which is the same tuple as (j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) 1); G_i(z) := G(z)_i ∈ ℝ; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ Euclid (m+1); for c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m, ins_i(c, y') := toLp (Fin.insertNth i c (ofLp y')). Q^d is the open unit cube of Euclid d. Hypotheses: (H1) G is C¹; (H2) G_i(y) = (−1)^i γ(Φ y)(E'_i) for all y and i; (H3) exteriorDerivative γ (Φ y) E = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m+1)) (fderiv ℝ G y) for all y.

1. Coordinates. G_i = proj_i ∘ G, where proj_i := EuclideanSpace.proj i is a continuous linear map. So each G_i is C¹ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.comp).

2. Trace as a divergence. Fix y and let D := fderiv ℝ G y. The orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m+1)) ℝ has i-th vector e_i, so LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner gives trace D = Σ_i ⟪e_i, D e_i⟫, and ⟪e_i, v⟫ = v_i (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). G is differentiable at y by (H1), so by the chain rule G_i = proj_i ∘ G has derivative proj_i ∘ D at y (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt.comp, HasFDerivAt.fderiv). Hence fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i = (D e_i)_i, and trace DG(y) = Σ_i fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i. With (H3), exteriorDerivative γ (Φ y) E = Σ_i fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i for every y.

3. Interchange of sum and integral. Rewrite the integrand on the left-hand side with step 2. For each i, cube_partial_ftc applied to (k, i, G) := (m, i, G_i), which is C¹ by step 1, says in its first conjunct that y ↦ fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i is integrable on Q^{m+1}. Hence integral_finsetSum gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} Σ_i fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i dy = Σ_i ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i dy. It remains to show, for each i, that the i-th summand equals the i-th summand of the claim.

4. One coordinate. Fix i. The second conjunct of the same instance of cube_partial_ftc gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i dy = ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(1, y')) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(0, y')) dy'. By (H2), G_i(ins_i(c, y')) = (−1)^i γ(Φ(ins_i(c, y')))(E'_i).

5. Faces of a face (parent step 1). For c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m, Φ(ins_i(c, y')) = a + c • w_i + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1. To see this, split Σ_{j ∈ Fin (m+1)} at i (Fin.sum_univ_succAbove _ i) and use (ins_i(c, y'))_i = c (Fin.insertNth_apply_same) and (ins_i(c, y'))_{succAbove i l} = y' l (Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove). Moreover toLp (fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)) = a + w_i: at k = ι i both coordinates are b_k + 1, and at k ≠ ι i both are b_k (Pi.single_eq_same, Pi.single_eq_of_ne, PiLp.single_apply). So with c = 1 (one_smul), Φ(ins_i(1, y')) = Φ¹_i(y') = toLp (fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)) + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1. With c = 0 (zero_smul, add_zero), Φ(ins_i(0, y')) = Φ⁰_i(y') = a + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1.

6. Constants. By steps 4 and 5, the i-th summand equals ∫_{Q^m} (−1)^i γ(Φ¹_i y')(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} (−1)^i γ(Φ⁰_i y')(E'_i) dy'. Pull (−1)^i out of both integrals (integral_const_mul) and factor it (mul_sub). The result is (−1)^i (∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ¹_i y')(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ⁰_i y')(E'_i) dy'), the i-th summand of the claim.

7. Summing over i (step 3) proves the identity. For m = 0 nothing changes: Q^0 = Euclid 0 is a single point of volume 1, each E'_i is the empty tuple, and the face integrals are evaluations at the two vertices. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each coordinate G_i = proj_i ∘ G is C¹.
trace DG(y) = Σ_i ⟪e_i, DG(y)e_i⟫ = Σ_i DG_i(y)e_i (trace_eq_sum_inner with basisFun, inner_single_left, chain rule), so by (H3) dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i ∂_iG_i(y).
cube_partial_ftc (first conjunct) gives integrability, so ∫ Σ_i = Σ_i ∫ (integral_finsetSum).
cube_partial_ftc (second conjunct): ∫_{Q^{m+1}} ∂_iG_i = ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(1,·)) − ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(0,·)), and (H2) turns G_i(ins_i(c,·)) into (−1)^i γ(Φ(ins_i(c,·)))(E'_i).
Faces of a face: Φ(ins_i(c, y')) = toLp(b) + c e_{ι(i)} + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} and toLp(b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) = toLp(b) + e_{ι(i)}.
Pull out (−1)^i (integral_const_mul, mul_sub) and sum over i.

subproblems.title: Integer regrouping of the signed faces of a lattice n-chain into a lattice (n−1)-chain
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P strictly increasing and b ∈ ℤ^P, and let β assign an integer to each pair. Then there are a finite set s' of pairs q = (ι', b') with ι' : Fin m → Fin P strictly increasing and b' ∈ ℤ^P, and integers β'_q, such that for every function I from pairs (ι', b') to ℝ: Σ_{p∈s} β_p Σ_{i∈Fin(m+1)} (−1)^i (I(ι∘succAbove i, b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) − I(ι∘succAbove i, b)) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q I(q), where 𝟙_{ι(i)} = Pi.single (ι i) 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (β : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℤ), (∀ p ∈ s, StrictMono p.1) → ∃ (s' : Finset ((Fin m → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (β' : (Fin m → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℤ), (∀ q ∈ s', StrictMono q.1) ∧ ∀ I : (Fin m → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℝ, ∑ p ∈ s, (β p : ℝ) * ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (I (p.1 ∘ Fin.succAbove i, p.2 + Pi.single (p.1 i) 1) - I (p.1 ∘ Fin.succAbove i, p.2)) = ∑ q ∈ s', (β' q : ℝ) * I q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 ("Regrouping") of the parent proof, with the strict-monotonicity remark of its step 1. The statement quantifies over an arbitrary I, so one (s', β') serves every test form; the parent applies it with I(q) := ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy. Purely finite bookkeeping: no analysis and no sibling is used.

Notation. For p = (ι, b) and i ∈ Fin (m+1): front(p, i) := (ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i, b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) and back(p, i) := (ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i, b). These are the parent's q(p, i, 1) and q(p, i, 0). [P] denotes 1 if P holds and 0 otherwise.

1. Choice of s'. Let s' := ⋃_{p ∈ s} ⋃_{i ∈ Fin (m+1)} {front(p, i), back(p, i)} (Finset.biUnion over s and Finset.univ). This is the image of the finite index set 𝒜 = s × Fin (m+1) × {0, 1} under κ(p, i, ε) = q(p, i, ε), as in the parent proof. In particular front(p, i) ∈ s' and back(p, i) ∈ s' for all p ∈ s and all i (Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton).

2. Choice of β'. Let β'(q) := Σ_{p ∈ s} Σ_{i} β_p (−1)^i ([front(p, i) = q] − [back(p, i) = q]) ∈ ℤ. This is the parent's fibre sum Σ_{a ∈ 𝒜, κ a = q} c(a) with c(p, i, ε) = β_p (−1)^i (2ε − 1), written with indicators.

3. Strict monotonicity. Let q ∈ s'. Then q = front(p, i) or q = back(p, i) for some p ∈ s and i, so q.1 = p.1 ∘ Fin.succAbove i. p.1 is strictly increasing by hypothesis and Fin.succAbove i is strictly increasing (Fin.strictMono_succAbove), so q.1 is strictly increasing (StrictMono.comp).

4. Each term picks out its two faces. Fix I, p ∈ s and i. Expanding the indicator difference (mul_sub, sub_mul, mul_ite, ite_mul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib), and using Σ_{q ∈ s'} [x = q] f(q) = f(x) for x ∈ s' (Finset.sum_ite_eq) together with step 1, we get Σ_{q ∈ s'} β_p (−1)^i ([front(p, i) = q] − [back(p, i) = q]) I(q) = β_p ((−1)^i (I(front(p, i)) − I(back(p, i)))).

5. Exchange of sums. By Finset.mul_sum and step 4, the left-hand side of the claim equals Σ_{p ∈ s} Σ_i Σ_{q ∈ s'} β_p (−1)^i ([front(p, i) = q] − [back(p, i) = q]) I(q). Exchanging the order of summation (Finset.sum_comm, twice) gives Σ_{q ∈ s'} Σ_{p ∈ s} Σ_i β_p (−1)^i ([front(p, i) = q] − [back(p, i) = q]) I(q). For each q, this inner double sum equals (β'(q) : ℝ) · I(q): the integer cast commutes with sums, products, powers and differences (push_cast, with ((−1 : ℤ)^i : ℝ) = (−1 : ℝ)^i and the cast of an indicator being the real indicator), and I(q) factors out (Finset.sum_mul). Hence Σ_{p ∈ s} β_p Σ_i (−1)^i (I(front(p, i)) − I(back(p, i))) = Σ_{q ∈ s'} β'(q) I(q).

6. Steps 1–5 give s' and β' with the required properties, and neither depends on I. For m = 0 nothing changes: each ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i is the unique map Fin 0 → Fin P, strict monotonicity is vacuous, and all sums are finite. ∎
proof_key_steps: front(p,i) = (ι∘succAbove i, b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}), back(p,i) = (ι∘succAbove i, b); s' := ⋃_{p,i} {front(p,i), back(p,i)}.
β'(q) := Σ_{p,i} β_p(−1)^i([front(p,i) = q] − [back(p,i) = q]), the parent's fibre sum.
q.1 = ι∘succAbove i is StrictMono (hypothesis, Fin.strictMono_succAbove).
For each (p, i) the q-sum over s' picks out its two faces (Finset.sum_ite_eq); exchange sums (Finset.sum_comm) and push the cast through to get Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q I(q).
